headline: New York Delivers $189M to Fight Summer Hunger for 1.6 Million Children
meta_description: New York State distributes $189 million in emergency food benefits to low-income children during summer break, addressing a critical annual gap in nutrition as…
summary_short: New York has reached 1.6 million low-income children with $189 million in summer food benefits, tackling the hunger crisis that emerges when school meals end.
body:
When schools close in June, millions of children lose access to the subsidized meals that sustained them through the academic year. New York Governor Kathy Hochul announced on July 1 that $189 million in Summer Electronic Benefits Transfer funds had already reached nearly 1.6 million low-income children across the state, with approximately $240 million expected to support around 2 million children by summer's end. Each eligible child receives $120 on an EBT card that functions like SNAP at authorized grocery stores and farmers markets—a lifeline that a USDA demonstration project found cuts very low food security among children by one-third.

The program's elegance lies in its simplicity and reach. Families already enrolled in SNAP, Public Assistance, or Medicaid receive the benefits automatically. Those not enrolled have until September 8, 2026, to apply online. Yet there's urgency: the $120 expires 122 days after issuance, meaning families must use it quickly. This structural gap—where "school meals disappear and budgets are stretched thin," in the words of Robin Hood's CEO Richard R. Buery Jr.—opens predictably every summer for low-income households already struggling with rising costs.

Beyond individual families, the spending circulates through neighborhoods. By allowing recipients to shop at local grocery stores and farmers markets, the program strengthens community economies. This commitment comes as federal nutrition programs face Republican-backed cuts in Congress, making New York's broader investment—$395 million to continue Universal Free School Meals through 2027, plus additional funding for food banks and nutrition assistance—a critical counter to federal retreat. The message is clear: summer hunger deserves the same urgency we give school-year nutrition.
quick_facts: $189 million reached 1.6 million children by early July
Each child receives $120 on an EBT card for groceries
Families already on SNAP get benefits automatically, no application needed
USDA study: summer benefits cut child food insecurity by one-third
